$comment: Source attribution manifest (M3.2). Metadata only — files are fetched by scripts/media/fetch-sources.mjs into the git-ignored media-src/ staging folder and pinned by sha256 in media/sources.lock.json. Every field below was taken from the source page on the access date; 'context' is what the archive says, not our interpretation.

sources.creator: Photographer not named. Published as a plate in Stinton Jones, 'Russia in Revolution' (1917); the title page says only 'Illustrated by unique photographs'.
sources.publishedIn: Stinton Jones, 'Russia in Revolution; being the experiences of an Englishman in Petrograd during the upheaval', London: Herbert Jenkins Ltd, © MCMXVII (1917); printed by Wm. Brendon and Son, Plymouth. Plate 'Soldiers with Red Flags Leading an Immense Crowd in the Nevsky Prospect', facing p. 136 (list of illustrations).
sources.sourceDate: Taken in Petrograd during the February Revolution (late Feb / early Mar 1917 Old Style = March 1917 New Style), per the book's context and the Commons date '1917-03'. Exact day unknown. First published 1917 in London.
sources.licence: Public domain in the United States (published 1917). Other jurisdictions: see rightsAnalysis — not asserted as worldwide public domain.
sources.licenceEvidence: Commons wikitext: {{PD-US}} only (no country-of-origin tag). Book © 1917 (title page).
sources.context: Book caption (list of illustrations): 'Soldiers with Red Flags Leading an Immense Crowd in the Nevsky Prospect'. Commons description (Spanish): 'Manifestación en el Nevsky Prospekt, Petrogrado, encabezada por soldados, marzo de 1917.' Our on-screen caption names neither place nor date ('Mùa đông · một thủ đô phương Bắc').
sources.attribution: Ảnh in trong sách của S. Jones, London 1917 (tác giả ảnh không rõ)
sources.archive: https://archive.org/details/russiainrevolut00jone (scan contributed by University of British Columbia Library; metadata: creator 'Jones, Stinton', publisher 'London : H. Jenkins limited', date 1917)

rightsAnalysis.US: Public domain: published 1917 (before 1929). Verified by publication date.
rightsAnalysis.UK (country of first publication): Probably expired, but not verified: photographer unidentified. For photographs taken before 1 June 1957 UK law keeps the 1911 Act term (50 years from the making of the negative → expired 1967); for works of unknown authorship the CDPA term is 70 years from making available (→ 1987). Residual uncertainty: if the photographer were identified, EU-term revival rules (1995 Duration Regulations) would need checking.
rightsAnalysis.Russia (where taken): Uncertain whether Russian law applies to a photo first published in the UK; for anonymous works published before 1943 Russian PD rules would apply. Not relied on.
rightsAnalysis.Vietnam (where the game is used): Photographic works are protected 75 years from first publication (Luật SHTT, Đ.27) → 1917 + 75 = 1992, expired — assuming Vietnamese law's term governs; not legal advice.
rightsAnalysis.unresolved: Photographer unknown; no UK archive record found; Commons carries only a US tag. Low residual risk; documented, not asserted as worldwide PD.
